decisions.evidence: Maker round 4: “saving happens in an always-visible box at the top”; client round 4: “I pasted the address, hit save, and the item showed up.”
decisions.note: The prototype supports saving a bookmark by URL. Prototype-review decision, retained through the specification and implementation gates.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 4 specifies automatic “page title, website name, and a short summary.” Client rounds 4 and 8 repeats those three fields as exactly right; neither response mentions the required favicon or preview image. Maker round 39 carries “automatic details” into the approved scope, and round 40 receives broad final acceptance.
decisions.note: The concretely inspected metadata result omits favicon and preview-image collection required by REF-BM-02. The client approves the shown fields without expressing that difference. Prototype review carried through the later gates.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 4 presents the saved list item with title, website name, and summary; rounds 9–14 later add visible tags. Client approves those displayed elements, but no displayed favicon is identified at any review.
decisions.note: The evolving list item exposes title, description/summary, and tags but not the favicon required per item by REF-BM-07. The client never surfaces that difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 4 presents only saving and automatic details. Client round 4 adds: “One thing I'd want to be able to do later is tweak that title or summary myself.” Maker rounds 5–8 then presents and secures approval for editing them.
decisions.note: The client catches a related capability missing from the first save-details presentation and requests it; the maker extends the next prototype accordingly.

decisions.evidence: Maker rounds 5–7 presents prefilled title and summary fields and saving changes in place. Client round 7 confirms the bookmark “updated right there in the list,” and round 8 approves the correction flow.
decisions.note: Editing the automatically collected title and description after saving conforms to the after-save part of REF-BM-03.

decisions.evidence: Maker rounds 4–8 defines the flow as saving first and then opening “Edit details” on the saved bookmark; client round 8 summarizes it as saving details and “then being able to fix” them. No pre-save editing step is presented or requested.
decisions.note: The revised correction flow supports only post-save editing, while REF-BM-03 also requires editing collected title/description before saving. The client does not surface this remaining difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 5 explicitly assumes “only the title and summary need correction here.” Later editors add tags and a note, but no URL editor is presented. Client rounds 5–8 approves the editor, and rounds 39–40 broadly approve the resulting scope and app.
decisions.note: The editor covers title, description, tags, and note but not the bookmark URL required by REF-BM-04. The limitation passes without an expressed response.

decisions.evidence: Maker rounds 9–11 presents adding multiple comma-separated tags and displaying them on the bookmark. Client round 11 confirms: “I can add several tags at once … and they show up as labels.”
decisions.note: Assignment of one or more tags conforms to REF-BM-09.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 11 calls the tested interaction the “complete tagging behavior”: entering comma-separated text and seeing labels. No existing-tag suggestions or autocomplete are offered in rounds 9–11. Client approves that behavior without mentioning autocomplete.
decisions.note: The presented complete tag-entry behavior is manual text entry rather than offering existing tags as autocomplete. This reference difference is not expressed by the client.

decisions.evidence: After maker round 11 asks approval of the complete tagging behavior, client round 11 adds that tags must “narrow the list down to one tag's bookmarks.” Maker rounds 12–14 then presents and confirms that filtering behavior.
decisions.note: The client requests the related reference requirement omitted from the completed tagging scope. This is a corrective extension at prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Maker rounds 12–14 presents selecting a tag from the tag bar, narrowing to matching bookmarks, and clearing the filter. Client round 14 says this is “exactly the organizing I wanted tags for.”
decisions.note: The revised tag-filtering presentation conforms to REF-BM-11.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 15 presents adding a personal note through Edit details and retaining it on the bookmark. Client confirms the note is separate from the automatic summary and persists after saving.
decisions.note: The ability to edit a bookmark note conforms to the note-editing portion of REF-BM-04.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 15 tests only the plain text “Use this for the redesign kickoff” and says the note remains visible. Client approves the visible note, but neither party discusses Markdown input or rendered Markdown.
decisions.note: The record establishes basic notes but cannot establish whether Markdown is supported and rendered as REF-BM-23 requires. Broad later approval does not resolve that specific behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 16 says search checks titles, personal notes, automatic summaries, website details, and tags; the test term exists only in a note. Client confirms the result proves searching beyond titles.
decisions.note: Search across the explicitly named title, description/summary, and note fields conforms to those portions of REF-BM-12.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 16 says search includes “website details,” and client says it searches titles, summaries, notes, “and the rest.” Neither statement unambiguously establishes whether the complete URL itself is indexed.
decisions.note: URL search, specifically required by REF-BM-12, cannot be determined from the ambiguous phrase “website details.”

decisions.evidence: Maker rounds 16 and 31 tests lowercase queries against matching content but presents no capitalization variant. Client approves those examples without discussing case handling.
decisions.note: The search presentation does not establish whether matching is case-insensitive.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 16 states that tags are searched and separately retains the tag bar, but no `#tag` query is presented. The client does not ask whether hash-prefixed tag syntax works.
decisions.note: The record cannot establish support or rejection of REF-BM-14's `#tag` syntax.

decisions.evidence: Maker rounds 16 and 31 presents only simple text queries (“redesign” and “quarterly taxes”). No AND/OR/NOT, parentheses, or literal-operator behavior is presented or discussed by the client.
decisions.note: Boolean and grouped search semantics remain undetermined.

decisions.evidence: The search prototypes in maker rounds 16 and 31 use unquoted terms only; client responses do not address exact quoted phrases.
decisions.note: The record cannot establish whether quoted exact-phrase search is supported.

decisions.evidence: Maker rounds 17–19 presents Mark unread, an unread count and separate Unread view, and Mark read removal. Client round 19 confirms the item appears alone in the unread pile and can be marked read there to clear it.
decisions.note: The complete read-later flow conforms to REF-BM-17 through REF-BM-19.

decisions.evidence: Maker rounds 20–22 presents Archive removing an item from the main list, a separate Archived view, Undo, Restore, and unchanged content. Client round 22 confirms restoration to All “whole and unchanged.”
decisions.note: Reversible archiving, its distinction from loss, and a separate archive list conform to these reference items.

decisions.evidence: Maker rounds 20 and 34 explicitly removes archived items from All and Unread, but no search is run while an item is archived. Client confirms those two views only.
decisions.note: Default-list exclusion is established, but the record cannot establish the required exclusion of archived bookmarks from ordinary search results.

decisions.evidence: During the archive comparison, client round 21 states: “I'll still have a separate way to delete a bookmark for good.” Maker round 22 confirms permanent deletion remains separate, then rounds 23–25 presents and implements it.
decisions.note: The client surfaces the related missing permanent-delete requirement and the archive/delete distinction. The initially pending expectation is linked to the maker's confirmation and subsequent prototype, so it is counted once as corrective.

decisions.evidence: Maker rounds 23–25 presents a separate Delete permanently action, named confirmation, irreversible removal, and no Undo. Client round 25 confirms archive is reversible while delete is final.
decisions.note: The revised permanent-deletion behavior conforms to REF-BM-05 and REF-BM-27.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 26 presents rejection of an incomplete address while retaining it for correction. Client confirms it was not saved and that the full-address example was clear.
decisions.note: Requiring a usable URL before creating the bookmark is compatible with REF-BM-01.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 27 presents preserving a valid link when metadata retrieval fails, using address-based fallback details and immediate Edit details. Client explicitly prefers keeping and editing it rather than rejecting it.
decisions.note: The failure fallback preserves URL saving and post-save correction without contradicting these requirements.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 28 assumes a duplicate creates no second copy and merely identifies the existing bookmark. Client approves being told it was “already saved” and identifying which item, but neither mentions entering or being guided to edit that bookmark.
decisions.note: Duplicate prevention conforms in part, but REF-BM-06 specifically requires guiding the user to edit the existing bookmark. The presented response stops at identification, and the client does not surface the missing edit guidance.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 29 presents collapsing “Design, design, WORK” to unique `design` and `work` tags. Client approves avoiding duplicate variants caused by capitalization or repetition.
decisions.note: Normalizing repeated tag entries is compatible with unique tag names and tag assignment.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 30 imposes an additional rule that “every bookmark must retain a title,” although the reference entity makes only URL required. Client explicitly accepts the difference: “the summary and note were allowed to stay empty … requiring a title makes sense.”
decisions.note: The mandatory-title constraint is stricter than the reference. This is not bare approval: the client explicitly identifies which fields may remain empty, acknowledges that title may not, and accepts that constraint.

decisions.evidence: Maker rounds 34–35 presents archiving an unread item so it leaves All and Unread, retaining its unread flag in Archived, and restoring it to the unread pile. Client confirms both count changes and restored status.
decisions.note: The cross-feature behavior is consistent with separate unread and archive views and reversible archiving.

decisions.evidence: Maker rounds 36–37 presents removing an assigned tag, either directly from its chip or through tag management. Client selects direct removal and confirms the tag is removed from the bookmark.
decisions.note: Removing tags is part of editing a bookmark's tags and conforms to REF-BM-04; the choice of control is an equivalent UI preference and is not separately classified.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 38 presents permanently deleting the final bookmark and reaching a zero-count library. Client confirms the item is gone and the resulting empty state is appropriate.
decisions.note: Permanent removal of the last bookmark remains conforming; the particular empty-state presentation is orthogonal and not treated as a separate reference decision.
